statement: For every n>=2 and gcd(2r+1,n)=1, the element [z^2,v]^r z^2 in the full completion of <z,v | v^2=1, [z^2,v]^n=1> is a square exactly for r=0 or -1 modulo n. The exact quotient maps apply this uniform obstruction to both normalized reflection labels of the standard one-section negative torus involution. Its full peripheral outer centralizer and normalizer are exactly the explicitly realized Klein four group; both standard negative conjugacy-orbit maps therefore have four-element fibres.
depends_on: D61 and D64 exact standard one-section extension and trivial IA centralizer; D62 all-unit and both-reflection-label transporters; D63 unique extension normalization; ordinary HNN and amalgam normal forms and their discrete Bass-Serre trees; Martino2007 Theorem3.7; explicit Heisenberg finite cover and the centralizer-closure argument proved here
manuscript_passages: Section 30, folios 194-196, scans 383-387; Section 31, folios 198-199 verso, scans 391-394; Part D(b), full loop-outer finite actions in type (1,1)
depends_on_doubtful_reading: None. Both discrete graph-of-groups presentation maps, the index-two torus cone subgroup, its actual finite surface cover, the completion comparison, and both normalized source labels are explicitly retained.
notes: The HNN extension has finite dihedral vertex group and identifies its two named reflection subgroups. The transporter c^r g has stable-letter length one. Its axis gives exact conjugacy to g only for r=0,-1, and the amalgam adjoining z with z^2=g has a unique transporter-fixed vertex for every other residue. Its discrete centralizer is exactly <c^r g>, using the unit condition to exclude the other dihedral vertex element. The index-two subgroup <X,Y | [X,Y]^n> has a degree n^3 closed surface cover from the finite Heisenberg quotient, proving the whole group virtually surface. Martino's primary theorem applies to every finite-index subgroup. The written direct hereditary-conjugacy-separability argument identifies the full completed centralizer with the closure of the discrete centralizer. The global exponent character sends the transporter to 2, proving its closure is the full Zhat and excluding a square by 2t=1. The finite quotient criterion forces mu modulo every 2n to be plus or minus one, and finite intersection couples these to a global sign. The second reflection label is compared by the exact inverse-and-conjugation formula for -mu. No exhaustion of all negative-involution conjugacy orbits is claimed.
computational_checks: code/part_c/standard_oneclass_square_d65.py and adjacent JSON/stdout check the exact free-product word identities, dihedral conjugacy and centralizer coefficients, and the Heisenberg covering monodromy and Euler characteristic. The full completion obstruction is proved using the exact centralizer and completion maps, not inferred from finite enumeration.
